intent.raw: Design the architecture for an ide-extension Chrome browser-extension lane with minimum overhead around the existing local HTML workbench.
intent.objective: Produce a governed design for a minimal Chrome MV3 side-panel extension that wraps the local ide-extension HTML workbench, mediates active browser tabs through content scripts, preserves kernel approval authority, and routes implementation to plan without claiming VS Code Integrated Browser control.
intent.operator_sentence: Use Invoke design to shape a minimum-overhead Chrome extension lane around the HTML workbench while preserving the kernel as authority and treating browser actions as approval-gated crossings.

subagent_strategy.explanation: This design was authored locally from concrete source artifacts; no delegated subagent fanout was needed.

stop_conditions: block if VS Code Integrated Browser control is treated as baseline evidence
flag if a needed source contract is missing

inputs.ref: bounded source contracts listed in DESIGN-TRANSPORT.md

stop_conditions: block if the extension becomes authority over approvals or receipts

gates.condition: browser-first extension design dispatch validates before plan handoff
Chrome extension remains adapter and local kernel owns approvals, durable state, and receipts
credentials, wallet/signature, payment, public-submit, destructive, and privileged browser actions are blocked or human-only in L0.5
this design dispatch creates plan-ready artifacts only; canonical vocabulary and implementation changes require a later owner-approved route
design includes context, structure, components, workflow, decisions, dependency interfaces, glossary consistency, and residue

boundaries.contract: Extension may observe and request typed browser actions; kernel owns grants, approvals, durable state, provider mediation, agent envelopes, and receipts.
boundaries.owner_boundary_check: extension is adapter, kernel is authority

boundaries.to_owner: human operator and local approval queue
boundaries.contract: Safe effectful browser actions require approval; hard-boundary and public-submit actions are blocked or performed directly by the human in L0.5.
boundaries.protected_action_mapping: credentials, wallet/signature, payment, public-submit, destructive, privileged browser actions

boundaries.contract: Design emits plan-ready handles and residue only; implementation edits require a later plan and task-session route.
boundaries.artifact_contract_bridge: architecture bundle, glossary consistency, layering seed, dispatch JSON, invoke result

authority.validation: dispatch-spec, existing smoke tests, future extension tests

receipts.producer: future Chrome extension background router and local kernel

state_namespaces.write_policy: store only local bridge override, transient UI preferences, and non-authoritative cache
durable approvals, events, artifacts, receipts, and workbench read model
typed actions only after policy and approval; hard boundaries blocked

promotion_guardrails: Dispatch validation checks route shape only.
Browser evidence can support the L0.5 extension lane only after witness tests pass.
Glossary, implementation, and lifecycle changes require owner-approved follow-up routes.
